461aaa80 · 8 files
The worker re-reads Kevin's private skills folder for workflow.json every 5 minutes, sends the catalog's hash on every heartbeat and the catalog itself only when the engine echoes another (an engine that echoes none gets it at most every 5 minutes). A lint failure is left out and logged by folder name. A kind workflow task's message names its skill and only that one, Kevin's words, the params text and declared params, the dated report file under %USERPROFILE%\.legion\reports\<workflow>\ (folder made by the worker), AGENT-RULES when present, and where it stops for Kevin's yes. Every finish appends one line to %USERPROFILE%\.legion\task-log.jsonl (request text stays on the laptop), pruned with the reports at 180 days. Tests never touch the real profile folder. 3afa3eca · 9 files
Replaces rulings R1 (14 shadow runs first) and R3 (proposals with Accept all). With LEGION_MEMORY_REVIEW=on every change that passes the code checks applies on the night: no shadow period, no confidence gate, retire and lasting-to-fading relabels included. - Cap per night is a setting, LEGION_MEMORY_REVIEW_CAP (default 25); changes over it leave no row and wait for the next night ("N left for tomorrow"). - Contradictions: a correction (distilled) applies on its own only to a distilled row (consolidation, review); against a row Kevin saved himself (manual, phone, web, claude) it waits in To check. - Undo: revert of a row a later night merged again undoes that later change first, so every row on Retired restores. A restored row is never changed on its own again; restored exact copies are not merged by code again. - The dismissal guard becomes an undo guard: over 30% of the last 14 runs' applied changes undone (at least 10) pauses on into shadow. - Kept: rows exist, live and the member's own; no added words; printed past dates; no identity numbers; retire never deletes; R4 evidence; the lock. - ADR 0067 amended, decisions.md entry, helper prompt, To check copy. no ticket
b97f0a1d · 14 files
The engine's remember (web assistant and /mcp) could write any memory, including one starting "Plan constraint: ", which the phone treats as a goal constraint; after web_search text only the prompt's wording defended it. Mirrors the phone's read-through gate. - Third-party tools: web_search and brief_latest (its news section is a search-grounded summary, the engine's get_sitrep). run_engine_tool notes one on the request before its handler, so a procedure step (morning_briefing) taints its own request too. vehicle_recalls and legion_docs stay out, as the phone's check_recalls does. - Web assistant: the browser counts turnComplete and sends `turn` with each tool call. A third-party tool marks (conversation, turn) in assistant_read_through_turns (Postgres, not the per-instance cache); remember in a marked turn is refused: "Not remembered: this turn read text from the web. Ask the user to confirm it in their own words next turn." No turn sent fails closed; a failed check refuses. - /mcp has no turn concept (stateless per request, no session), so the narrowest rule: it, and a web call naming no conversation, may not write a memory starting "Plan constraint:". Everything else unchanged. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdhBqotr4WfNvLT28yi1rF

fix(claude-session): warm builds for worker tasks, through the laptop's Gradle lock
alfred-builds 08
53e6b028 · 11 files
Task 7's first compile in a fresh per-task worktree took 23 min 56 s of its 30 minute cap. Three causes: a new worktree with no build outputs, `gradlew --stop` after every build_lock run (so every task started a cold daemon), and nothing shared between tasks. - warm_worktree.py: one persistent worktree, work\warm\wt. `claim --task N --branch B` resets it to the base (checkout -f -B, clean -fd, anything left uncommitted stashed first) and keeps the ignored build outputs, so the next compile is incremental. One task holds it at a time (a lease in the worker root, which helpers cannot write); a needs_confirmation task keeps it up to 6 h for the follow-up that ships it, which inherits it; the worker releases it when a task finishes any other way. Busy: exit 3 and the helper uses a fresh worktree as before. `prepare` seeds it with one compile. - ship.py run on the warm tree takes the lease first and refuses in words if another task holds it, so a ship never checks out a branch under another task's helper. - build_lock.py: never `--stop` (Kevin's laptop rule; the stable private registry keeps the daemon for the next task until Gradle's idle timeout); every Gradle step adds `--max-workers=1 --build-cache` and also takes the laptop's shared mkdir lock (config `gradle_lock`, default the lock g.sh uses), so worker builds and every other agent's Gradle run one at a time. A lock a killed worker build left is cleared once its pid is gone; anyone else's is only waited for. JAVA_HOME falls back to Android Studio's JBR like ship.py. - Prompt rule 12 tells helpers both: claim the warm worktree, and Gradle only via build_lock (shared lock, one worker, never --stop, a long build is waited for, not worked around). Measured 2026-11-09 under the shared lock, --max-workers=1, in task 7's already-built worktree: compileDebugKotlin with a cold daemon 18 s, with a warm daemon 2 s; compiling the unit tests and running the Snake tests 5 min 16 s (25 of 25 pass). Configuration cache stored and reused cleanly there but is left off until assembleFast is checked with it. fix(claude-session): a helper paused on its own build has not ended
no ticket
4414be55 · 4 files
Task 7 (2026-11-06) failed with "The helper stopped without reporting a result" 60 s after the CLI's `completed` notification for a helper that had only parked on its own background compile; its real report 13 minutes later was dropped as "not running". Measured on CLI 2.1.319 (2026-11-09 probe): the raw stream-json task_notification is the same for a pause and for the end (no interim flag; `summary` is the helper's own text). What differs is live children: their task_started carries parent_task_id/owned_by_subagent, and background_tasks_changed lists them. So: - `completed` is recorded, then judged after settle_s: live background work owned by the helper (any depth) means paused, and only the 30 minute cap applies; none means ended. - A helper's task_started again (the CLI resuming it) clears the end state. A child's task_started never replaces the helper, even when its description names the task. - Ended with no report: after report_grace_s the main window gets one `[report N]` reminder to run report.py from the helper's last result; still nothing after another grace, the task fails in words. killed/failed keep the 60 s grace. - A report that arrives after the worker failed the task replaces the failure while it is still in the outbox; once delivered it is kept in reports/late (the engine's FinishView refuses a second finish with 409), never silently dropped. fake_claude.py emits the 2.1.319 shapes (pause, children, background_tasks_changed, resume) and answers reminders; tests cover pause-not-failed, question after a pause, cap while paused, reminder answered, reminder unanswered, and both late-report paths. The ask_mail router was handed no date, so "today" had nothing to anchor an after: to, and "new" could fall to the blank-query briefing (unread, Primary only), which hides mail already opened elsewhere or filed under Updates. GmailToolLogic.routeDateClause appends the clock (UTC offset, never a zone id) and today's and yesterday's local midnights in epoch seconds, because the Gmail API reads after:YYYY/MM/DD as Pacific midnight. LEGION_DEMO_MAX_SESSION_MINUTES (default 5, 1-30) is both what a mint reserves and how long a recruiter's Live token lives: assistant/session.py sets expireTime = mint + 5 min for a recruiter (members keep 30). After expireTime Google rejects the session's messages but only "may" close the socket (API reference AuthToken.expireTime, quoted in web-assistant research 01), so the browser also ends the conversation: LiveOptions.sessionLimit arms a timer at the token's expires_at, and /try passes "Demo sessions last 5 minutes. Start another any time." for a visitor only. VOICE_MINT_MINUTES (10) is gone. openapi.yaml and schema.d.ts: expires_at help text only, no shape change. recruiter-demo 04: global daily demo budget, reserved before a recruiter mint
recruiter-demo 04
e5f83bec · 9 files
DemoBudgetDay holds one UTC day's reserved cents. A recruiter's Live mint reserves 10 minutes at the per-minute rate in one conditional UPDATE against budget minus the text reserve, and gets 429 "Today's demo budget is used up. Try again tomorrow." when it does not fit; a mint Google refuses gives its reservation back. Members never touch the budget. charge_text_call (full budget) is built and tested but unwired: the web's typed chat rides the same Live mint, and a text-only Live setup is not adopted (see demo/budget.py). Settings LEGION_DEMO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD (5), LEGION_DEMO_TEXT_RESERVE_USD (1), LEGION_DEMO_COST_PER_VOICE_MINUTE_USD (0.10), LEGION_DEMO_COST_PER_TEXT_CALL_USD (0.01), defaults reasoned in demo/budget.py. Concurrency test races 12 mints at a 3-mint cap. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01J2sDBYR9hMDRn7hjB88o9B

recruiter-demo 05: a recruiter's assistant is Alfred, addressed to a stranger, and greets
recruiter-demo 05
91ce8a49 · 4 files
A recruiter always gets Alfred with the persona's own voice, the same companion the web resolves for Kevin with no row overriding it; no stored row can change it. The prompt adds a visitor register (no first name, no "sir", no teasing), a demo frame (Kevin's LEGION on a made-up household), and a first-turn greeting naming four things the recruiter's tools can do. A Live setup carries no turns, so the browser's opening text turn is the cue, as the phone's beginConversation opener is. Members' prompts are unchanged.
